opportunities.title: JMD Currency Precision — Full-Stack Fix
opportunities.description:
---

#### Background
Flash is a Bitcoin banking platform for Jamaica. Users who have set JMD as their display currency are seeing incorrect amounts across three critical surfaces: their wallet balance, the send/receive flows, and their transaction history. These are not cosmetic issues — users are losing money on precision truncation and seeing a transaction history that changes every time the BTC price moves.

The bugs span the full stack. The backend serves stale/wrong data from its transaction adaptor layer, and the mobile app compounds the problem with its own conversion errors. Both must be fixed for JMD amounts to be trustworthy end-to-end.

---

#### Scope

This bounty covers all three affected surfaces:

Wallet Balance


The BTC wallet balance query (me.btcWallet.balance) currently returns a serialized class object ({}) instead of a number, because BtcWallet.balance serializes the WalletBalance class instance rather than its numeric value.

File: src/graphql/shared/types/object/btc-wallet.ts (~line 49)
Fix: Return Number(balance.asCents(8)) — the raw satoshi count as a number.
---

Send & Receive Flows

## Context

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $70] Add endpoint-level failure-injection tests for the retry path
opportunities.description:
## Context

`README.md:51-52` states plainly that the retry path has been exercised by hand rather than by an automated failure-injection test. `tests/retry_test.ts:44-80` tests `withRetry` in isolation and `tests/indexer_orchestration_test.ts:392-415` only covers a permanent DB failure; nothing verifies that a transient failure recovering on the second attempt yields a successful run with the checkpoint advanced exactly once and no failure row.

## Proposed Change

Add endpoint-level tests using the scripted RPC/stub client that fail once or twice then succeed, asserting eventual 200, completed writes, a single checkpoint advance, and no `indexer_runs` failure row.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A transient `getEvents` failure followed by success yields `status: 'ok'` and no failure row
- A transient DB `upsert` failure followed by success behaves the same
- A permanently failing dependency leaves the checkpoint untouched and records exactly one failure
- Tests use the injected `sleep` so they run without real delays

opportunities.title: check_contrast.py: add --json output and a CI action that fails on contrast regressions
opportunities.description:
## Problem
`check_contrast.py --matrix` is the one part of tastemaker that is a computation rather than judgment, but its output is human-readable text only. That means nothing downstream can consume it: a project can't fail CI when a palette change breaks a text-safe pairing, and the agent has to re-parse prose to update the style lock.

## Proposal
1. Add a `--json` flag to `skills/tastemaker/scripts/check_contrast.py` (all three modes: pair, `--palette`, `--matrix`). For `--matrix`, emit every pair with its ratio and class (`text-safe` / `ui-safe` / `decorative`), plus the grouped legal pairings.
2. Exit non-zero when a pairing that the style lock marks as text-safe drops below 4.5:1.
3. Ship a small composite GitHub Action (e.g. `.github/actions/contrast-check`) that reads the palette from `.tastemaker/style-lock.md` and runs the check on PRs.

## Acceptance
- `--json` output is stable and documented in the script's docstring.
- Existing text output is unchanged without the flag.
- A PR that lowers a text-safe pair below 4.5:1 fails the action with the offending pair named.

---
💰 This issue has a **MergePay** bounty in USDC on Arc. See it on https://mergepay.fun/app#bounties

opportunities.title: [Bug] Transaction history adaptor shows wrong settlement display price for JMD users
opportunities.description:
## Summary

The transaction history adaptor (`src/app/wallets/get-transactions-for-wallet.ts`) serves incorrect display amounts for JMD users. Since Ibex IS the ledger and Flash has no server-side ledger for Ibex-settled transactions, this adaptor is the **only place** to fix display amounts — if it's wrong, every historical transaction displays wrong, retroactively.

## The Bugs

### 1. Hardcoded USD instead of user display currency
The adaptor returns `USD` as the display currency and does not convert the settlement amount to the user's configured currency (JMD). This means both the currency label and the numeric value are wrong — JMD users see raw USD amounts labeled as their display currency. One fix: pass the user's display currency into the adaptor and apply the conversion.

### 2. Wrong offset in pagination/conversion
An offset error causes transactions to map to incorrect price points, shifting which rate gets applied to which transaction.

### 3. `Math.floor` truncates fractional amounts
`Math.floor` on converted amounts silently drops fractional JMD cents. For small BTC transactions, this can truncate the display amount to `0`.

## Why This Matters

- Flash has **no serve

opportunities.title: [FEATURE] Gifting & Referral Reward Credit System
opportunities.description:
## Request Type
Feature Request

## User Story
As a **growth marketing team**, I want to **enable subscription gifting and automated referral rewards** so that **existing customers drive new customer acquisition through word-of-mouth and we incentivize viral growth**.

## Problem Statement
SaaS platforms miss growth opportunities without referral programs:
- **No Viral Loop:** Satisfied customers can't easily share product
- **Manual Gifting:** No way to gift subscriptions for holidays/special occasions
- **Lost Word-of-Mouth:** Can't track or incentivize customer referrals
- **Expensive CAC:** Customer Acquisition Cost stays high without referral channel
- **Missed Occasions:** Birthdays, holidays, graduations = gifting opportunities

Industry data shows:
- Referred customers have 16% higher LTV than non-referred
- Referral programs can reduce CAC by 50-70%
- 83% of satisfied customers willing to refer, but only 29% do (lack of easy mechanism)
- Gift subscriptions convert to paid at 40-60% rate after gift expires

Without gifting/referrals:

opportunities.title: Work list: run Control Tower and BashArena with glovebox on the Flamingo cluster
opportunities.description:
This is a **work list** (CLAUDE.md § What gets an issue, type 6). It is the one tracker for this milestone. Add a row by editing this body, and tick a row in the PR that lands it.

## What cannot be done today

The Control Tower (LinuxArena) eval runs only on a GitHub runner that has `/dev/kvm` and a Docker daemon. The driver boots each cell's microVM from that host, builds the env's images with the host's Docker, and judges an attack by reading the host's egress decision log. A Flamingo pod has none of that. It gets a microVM from the node through `runtimeClassName: glovebox`, but it cannot run Docker, and its outgoing traffic is not filtered yet.

```text
today:  GitHub runner -> glovebox sandbox -> Kata microVM, host egress log judges the attack
wanted: Inspect runner -> pod with runtimeClassName: glovebox on a Flamingo node,
        node-side egress log judges the attack
```

This matters because a guarded cell on Flamingo today has no egress allowlist. Its attack-success number would measure an open network, not glovebox.

BashArena has no harness or setting pin in this tree.

## Done when

- [ ] A free provisioning run (`ct_e2e_agent_model: ctscript/submit`) over every pinned

opportunities.title: Epic: use classification and deterministic code where generic prompting is wasteful

## Outcome

Brain-kit uses deterministic code for mechanical operations, a bounded classifier (Jev) for suitable semantic decisions, and LLM generation only where it adds value. Each candidate gets a recorded go/no-go. Accepted changes are implemented through scoped follow-up tasks attached here.

## The question every candidate answers

**Can code and/or a bounded classifier match or beat the current LLM/agent path on quality and reliability for this task?**

Cost is not measured. A bounded judgment or deterministic code is assumed cheaper than a generative call, so a candidate whose quality and reliability are on par or better is a go. The evaluation exists to establish feasibility, reliability and quality. Shipped product cost tracking is unaffected.

## Lean evaluation protocol (maintainer ruling, 2026-10-10)

1. **Arms, all on identical inputs:**
   - **Current path:** the shipped skill, prompt or command, run against the real model it uses today (`claude-sonnet-5-5` unless the product path uses another).
   - **Candidate:** code plus Jev (`jev-1.13.0`) Choice, Noul or Score judgments.
   - **Deterministic baseline:** any existing code-only baseline.
2. **Cases:** fictional Od

## Summary

Flash currently requires a working connection to IBEX APIs (sandbox and production) for basic app functionality. If IBEX APIs are unreachable, users experience degraded or broken flows that should otherwise work independently.

## Goal

The app should function with **BTC-only wallet capabilities** when IBEX APIs are unavailable. USD wallet features can gracefully degrade, but core BTC functionality must not depend on IBEX.

## Requirements

- [ ] App startup must succeed without IBEX API connectivity
- [ ] BTC wallet (balance, send, receive) must work independently of IBEX
- [ ] USD wallet features should gracefully degrade (show unavailable state, not crash/error)
- [ ] Transaction history should display BTC transactions regardless of IBEX status
- [ ] Error handling should clearly distinguish between Flash-native failures and IBEX dependency failures
